stack/tokens: So far, one token asked at a time. Self-attention lets every token ask at once. Say there are T tokens: stack them as the rows of a matrix, X, T by d.
stack/qkv: Each token's query becomes one row of a matrix, Q; its key, one row of K; its value, one row of V. So Q and K are T by d k, and V is T by d v, where d v is each value's length.
stack/scores: Then one matrix product scores every query against every key: Q times K transpose. T by d k, times d k by T, gives T by T.
stack/entry: Entry i, j is token i's query dotted with token j's key, divided by the square root of d k. Row two, column zero: how much fish looks at cats.
mix/softmax: Softmax runs along each row, giving the weights, A. Every row adds up to one: it is how one token splits its attention over all of them.
mix/fish: Here fish, row two, gives a half to cats and a quarter each to like and to itself.
mix/out: Then A times V. T by T, times T by d v, gives T by d v: one output row per token.
mix/row: Row two of the output is the weighted sum of the rows of V: half of two and zero, plus a quarter of zero and four, plus a quarter of four and four. That is two and two.
mix/formula: All of self-attention in one line: softmax of Q K transpose over the square root of d k, times V.
